notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.6.12.3 SR2: "Routine-name-1 is a COBOL word and it may be referred to only in an ENTER sentence." Implemented: enterOperand takes one word token for routine-name-1, so a literal or an integer is a syntax error, and because BindStatementCore binds ENTER as BoundNop and declares nothing, a word that is only a routine-name resolves nowhere else: GO TO, PERFORM, MOVE, CALL and DISPLAY of it are refused with COBOL1639 (the witness is the GO TO). Not implemented, both because routine-name-1 is a bare token that never reaches the cobolWord rule or the user-defined word census: (1) routine-names are one of the disjoint sets of user-defined words (§1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1: "All user-defined words, except segment-numbers and level-numbers, can belong to one and only one of these disjoint sets"), but UserWordKind has no routine-name member, so a word written as routine-name-1 and also declared as a paragraph-name or a data-name is referred to outside the ENTER sentence with no diagnostic, although the same check refuses a data-name that is also a paragraph-name (COBOL2692); (2) "is a COBOL word": VisitCobolWord asks the 30-character limit of §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 (COBOL1567) and the reserved-word screen only of cobolWord, so a routine-name of 31 or 38 characters and the reserved words LINKAGE and COBOL are accepted as routine-name-1 at 85 (so is a 31-character language-name-1). The verdict stands while ENTER is accepted at 85; the owner question on 1985-SR-VI.6.12.3-1 may remove the statement.

next.reason: 1985: "Routine-name-1 is a COBOL word and it may be referred to only in an ENTER sentence."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the ENTER statement; the statement and routine-name-1 are dropped.". No 2023 clause holds the ENTER feature, and no worded candidate covers routine-name-1 or the ENTER sentence. The statement is absent from 2023, so the rule is dropped.
